trans-unit.target: Click "Connect" on the "Bluesky" tile, then grant access on Bluesky. The site stores the session by itself.
Last, if you wish, search for "social-bluesky-handle" in the configuration and name the linked account: the next connection will offer it at once. Left empty, you will pick it on Bluesky's page.
To change a post's date, drag it onto a coming time of the week, or onto a day of the month where it keeps its time: it is planned there, approved or not as before.
To write a post, click "New post", or double-click straight on the time or the day it should go out: the post's screen opens with that moment already filled in.

The panel takes you to the calendar: the week of your posts, those gone out and every coming one at its date and time, red to approve, green approved. Its start and end hours are set in the configuration.
Click a post on the calendar: its panel changes its date and time, approves it or takes it back to a draft, or opens its texts to edit them.
In the left-hand column, the "Social" submenu leads to "Connections": each network has its tile there, with its state and its "Connect" button.
Click "Connect" on the "Google Business Profile" tile, then grant access with the Google account owning the listing. The site stores the token, the account and the listing by itself.

Search for "social-google-oauth-client-id" and "social-google-oauth-client-secret" in the settings list, and paste in the two values taken from the Google Cloud console. The secret only shows after a click on "Show sensitive data". The token, the account and the listing will fill themselves in at the next step.
Finally, on the page of your choice, add a collection block and pick the customer reviews source. The reviews are shown with their rating, their date and the link to the original review.

This first part does not happen on the site but at Google, and it takes seven to ten business days: request access to the Business Profile API, then publish the OAuth app. The help procedure "Display your listing's Google reviews" gives the links and the exact order. Come back here once access is granted.

On a review's row, the arrow button opens the public reply, which goes to Google as soon as it is saved. The text and the rating belong to their author: neither can be edited nor deleted. An abusive review is reported to Google.

The panel takes you to the reviews screen, which gathers every review the site holds, whatever the platform. Google's come in on their own every night: the list stays empty until the first synchronization has run.

The rest happens without you: the reviews come in every night, the synchronization task being scheduled by the bundle itself. Only one optional key is left, "social-google-listing-url", the public address of the listing, carried into the site's structured data.
Click "Connect" on the "LinkedIn" tile, then grant access with the profile's LinkedIn account. The site stores the token and the profile by itself.
Search for "social-linkedin-client-id" and "social-linkedin-client-secret" in the settings list, and paste in the app's two values.

This first part happens at LinkedIn: create an app attached to a Page you administer, add it the sharing and sign-in products, and declare the site's return address. Come back here with the ID and the secret.
Right after comes the box showing the network's name. Uncheck it and the name leaves the screen, but screen readers keep reading it: it leaves the display, never the accessibility.
Click the button at the top of the screen: "Create" if the list does not exist yet, "Edit" if it is already there. There is only one for the whole site.
At the bottom of the form you find the list of networks. Add one row per network: its icon, the address of your page over there, and a label if you want to replace the network's own.

Move down to the icon style. You can pick the plain icon, the badge in the network's own colors, the ring filling in on hover, or text only. The preview right below shows the result without waiting for a save.
The first field is the introduction, the text editor at the top of the form. Write a line inviting visitors to follow you, or leave it empty: nothing at all will then be rendered.

Let's start with the links to your networks. The panel takes you to the social links screen, in the left-hand column: your networks are not page content, you enter them once here and the site picks them up everywhere.
All that is left is to put the social links block on a page or in the footer: wherever it sits, this is the list it renders.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
Click "Connect" on the "Facebook & Instagram" tile, then grant access with the Facebook account managing the Page. The site stores the Page, its token and the Instagram account by itself.

Search for "social-meta-app-id" and "social-meta-app-secret" in the settings list, and paste in the app's two values. If the account manages several Pages, fill in "social-meta-page-id" too, or the first one will be taken.

This first part happens at Meta, on developers.facebook.com: create an app, add Facebook Login to it with the site's return address, and leave it in development mode. Check too that the Page is linked to the Instagram professional account. Come back here with the ID and the secret.
Back on the list, "Approve" hands the post over to its planned date: it goes out on its own, instead of being sent at once.
The edit button opens the post: one text per network, each at the length that network accepts, under the photos or the video going out with it. Correct what needs to be.
Add photos or a video here, in the order they go out, or take some from the gallery with "Add from the site". Each ticked network's rules are checked when saving.
"Send on" picks this post's networks: untick one not to post there, tick one to get a text written for it.
The panel takes you to the posts screen. Each has its date and time; those in draft wait here for your reading, then your approval.
The "Planned for" field sets the date and time the post goes out once approved, to the quarter of an hour.
"From an address" prepares a draft of any page, of this site or another one, at the date you choose.
Back on the list, the paper-plane button sends the post to every network that has not taken it yet. A network refusing keeps its message, and another click tries it again.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
"Generate a series" prepares several drafts at once, at a steady pace, which you read and then approve together.
Choose the pace: one draft a day, a week or a month.
Click "Generate the drafts": the calendar opens on the first one, leaving only the proofreading and the approval.
If you wish, add a photo or a video: it goes out with every post written here.
Choose where the texts come from: one text, an instruction the AI varies, or the site's next contents.
The panel takes you to the generation of a series: several drafts at once, which you will proofread afterwards. Say how many, from when and on which networks.
The anchor field is optional. A short id, "share" for instance, lets a menu entry point straight at the band. Without an anchor, it is still reached by scrolling the page.
Finally open any published page: the buttons are there, with the look you have just given them. Hovering the band raises a button bringing you straight back to this screen.
The next box shows or hides the "share this page" line above the buttons. Its wording is the site's own: only its display is set here.
Click the button at the top of the screen: "Create" if they do not exist yet, "Edit" otherwise. There is only one set of buttons for the whole site.
Then the fill. The preview right below updates on every change, before anything is even saved.
The first list is the networks. Tick the ones you want to offer, then drag them into place: the order of the list is the one your visitors will see.
The share buttons show on your pages. What we set here is which ones show and what they look like; if a warning says they are disabled, turn them back on first. The panel takes you to their screen.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
Below, pick the shape: wide, square or round button. That is the room the buttons will take under your pages.
"Share buttons" sets the buttons placed under your pages: which networks, in which order and what they look like.
"Calendar" shows the calendar of your posts: those gone out, and every coming one at its date. Drag one onto another time to move it.
"Connections" gathers the networks the site connects to, each on its tile: connected or not, and the button that connects it.
"Social networks" holds the list of your networks, one for the whole site, rendered wherever the social links block is put.
"Posts" gathers your posts, written here or prepared: you read each text, then you approve or publish.
